abstract: Signaling mechanisms are used in various types of matching markets so that applicants may credibly signal interest in firms. They have been observed to improve outcomes in job markets and dating markets, and proven to improve outcomes in several stylized theoretical models. In this paper we develop optimal signaling mechanisms for a simple one-round matching market consisting of $n$ applicants and $n$ firms. We consider a much richer space of signals than have been used previously, in theory or practice, and also consider randomized signaling mechanisms, which have not been systematically studied. For each $k \geq 1$, we determine the optimal deterministic and randomized signaling mechanisms in which applicants signal $k$ firms. In the limit as $k\to \infty$, our deterministic mechanism guarantees that in expectation, $\approx 75.4504\%$ of the applicants receive job offers, and this is optimal. Likewise, for $k \to \infty$, our randomized mechanism guarantees that $\approx 78.197\%$ of the applicants receive offers, which is also optimal. The optimal $k$-signal randomized mechanism is non-constructive, and has a rather complex description. We describe some simple randomized signaling mechanisms whose efficiency surpasses that of the limiting optimal deterministic mechanism. Finally, we also discuss incentive-compatibility for the firms to follow the mechanism.

title: Optimal Signaling Mechanisms for One-round Matching Markets
